The GNP and ZnO were mechanically homogenized using planetary ball milling (PBM) at a ratio of 1:1.
The crystallite size of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites was 19.3 nm, with a crystallinity percentage of 81.8%.
The GNP/ZnO nanocomposites exhibited the lowest reflection loss of -28.21 dB at 8.45 GHz and a through power of 99.84% when the thickness was 3 mm.
FE-SEM images showed that the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites formed a disordered crystallite layered-structure material.
XRD analysis confirmed the presence of distinct crystallite peaks of ZnO and the carbon peak of GNP in the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites.
FTIR analysis revealed the presence of carbon bonds and oxygen-containing functional groups in the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites.
The decreasing crystallite size and crystallinity percentage of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites, compared to the individual materials, led to a larger surface area and enhanced polarization.
The disordered crystallite layered-structure of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites facilitated dielectric loss, interface, and dipole polarization, improving the microwave absorption performance.
The GNP/ZnO nanocomposites outperformed the individual GNP and ZnO materials in terms of microwave absorption properties.
The paper highlighted the potential of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites as advanced lightweight functional materials for future stealth aircraft applications in the military sector.
The primary objective of utilizing PBM was to modify the particles, in particular to reduce the particle size of the materials, which increases the surface area and promotes polarization.
The layered carbon sheets of GNP were observed in the FE-SEM images, indicating the successful incorporation of GNP in the nanocomposites.
The XRD pattern of ZnO exhibited a hexagonal crystal system and a wurtzite crystal type, confirming the purity of the ZnO material.
The GNP/ZnO nanocomposites showed strong microwave polarization capabilities, leading to the excellent microwave absorption performance.
The through power of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites was calculated to be 99.84%, indicating their high efficiency in microwave absorption.
